one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban explains the context of CJ Sereno's widely quoted remark about retiring in 2030 -- she was responding to his own introduction at the FLP Professorial Chairs launch on September 18 at the Metrobank Auditorium, in which he expressed his hope to be alive at 93 for her retirement ceremony and to see her bequeath a 'transparent, accountable, excellent and trustworthy judiciary.' In her extemporaneous response, Sereno projected a judiciary that is 'the best sector in the bureaucracy' with world-class, internationally accredited systems. The column then summarizes her four reform pillars: (1) Predictability -- cases with the same facts and issues decided the same way regardless of ponente or composition, rules not changed midstream; (2) Rationality -- citizens can detect the logic and sensitivity behind decisions; (3) Speed -- cases have 'windows of opportunity' and must be decided within their time frame or become academic; and (4) Responsiveness -- issues addressed squarely, clearly, and forcefully. The FLP launch honored its first seven professorial chair holders (JJ Azcuna and Nachura; Deans Bautista, Candelaria, Concepcion, Diokno, and Divina), with Candelaria delivering his first FLP lecture at ADMU the next day on IMF and post-WW2 developmental agencies. The column connects this to the Global Forum on Liberty and Prosperity (October 18-20, 2006, Makati) -- attended by 300+ jurists from six continents at the end of the author's term -- where Canadian CJ McLacklin proposed the philosophy be titled in full as 'liberty and prosperity under the rule of law.'
